title: The album From Austin High Comes Jazz
summary: Freeman recommends the 1938 New York Condon-group album with Tough and Teagarden that he fronted.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And when you think of that alone, or even if it had only been fifteen years, that is still a long time, still way ahead of his... And I think that when you suggested earlier that there isn't enough said about Dave, I certainly must agree with that, that I would like to suggest that fans go back to an album that Dave and I made, it's called from -- I think it's called From Austin High Comes Jazz or simply called Comes Jazz, and we used the Condon, Pete and Russell, group: Pee Wee Max Kaminsky, Eddie himself, we had Jack Teagarden, because Jack sings that thing, 'Jack Hits the Road,' blues, and if you just listen to Dave Tough on that, that is the finest -- I mean, how they managed to get it recorded so beautifully. John Hammond handled that date, tape, by the way.
No, it was done in New York, about 1938 -- the end of '38, and maybe into '39. It was a marvelous album called Jazz Band Tunes, and the way Dave Tuft plays drum on that --
What did that come out on, was it Columbia?
I think it was Columbia. I am not sure.
I am glad you mentioned that.
I think it is called Comes Jazz. And it is fronted by me, although it had been Condon's group which, I fronted.
